title: Coral and the Recipe
premise: Hazel Voss arrives at Saltline Academy, a school built on the ruins of a drowned fishing village, carrying five years of grief and hypervigilance after her family's collapse. When her only friend, Marisol, vanishes leaving a ring of antique keys, Hazel discovers the school's founding recipe — a brine-cured bread said to hold the memories of the town's founders — and realizes Marisol was tracing the recipe's stolen, scattered pages. As Hazel follows the keys through the school's sealed spaces, she uncovers that the administration erased the village's history to protect its own legacy, and that Marisol's family were the recipe's original keepers. In the climax, Hazel recovers the final page from the flooded archive beneath the gymnasium, nearly drowning in the process, and chooses to bake the bread publicly at graduation, restoring the town's memory and forcing the truth into the open. Marisol returns — having gone into hiding to protect her grandmother — and Hazel, no longer careful to the point of hurting, claims a place in the tradition she helped save.
about_author: Casper Eriksen is the pen name of a writer who grew up in a coastal town where the high school parking lot covered the foundations of a cannery, and who has spent years collecting the recipes and rumors locals refused to write down. This is their second novel for young adults, following a debut praised for its salt-stung atmosphere and stubborn, tender protagonists.

chapters.title: The New Kid Counts the Exits
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On her first day at Saltline Academy, Hazel maps every exit, cataloging dangers out of five-year-old habit. She meets Marisol Reyes, who breaks through her defenses with blunt kindness and a shared lunch table in the boiler room. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness cracking open into cautious hope.

chapters.title: Bread and Salt
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol shows Hazel the school's odd founding tradition: a ceremonial loaf baked from the 'Founders' Recipe,' displayed but never eaten. Marisol confesses her grandmother claims the recipe was stolen from her family. Emotional beat: the thrill of sharing a secret, and the first hint of a larger wrong.

chapters.title: Five Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A flashback woven through a school assembly: Hazel recalls her family's unraveling and why she stopped trusting institutions. She watches the headmaster perform the bread ceremony and notices his hands shake. Emotional beat: dread surfacing — the ceremony is a performance covering something rotten.

chapters.title: The Ring of Keys
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Marisol doesn't come to school. At her locker, Hazel finds a ring of seven antique keys with a note: 'If I'm gone, they took the pages.' The school calls it a runaway case. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fusing — Hazel's carefulness finally has a purpose.

chapters.title: Key One: The Trophy Case
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The first key opens a display cabinet in the administration wing, where Hazel finds a 1910s photograph of the drowned village — and Marisol's great-grandmother standing in front of the bakery. Emotional beat: grief-tinged wonder as the erased history begins to surface.

chapters.title: Key Two: The Boiler Room
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, in flashbacks. Through Marisol's hidden notebook stashed in their lunch spot, Hazel learns Marisol's investigation: the recipe's original pages were split and hidden when the school absorbed the village land. Emotional beat: intimacy with an absent friend, reading her voice in every margin.

chapters.title: Key Three: The Headmaster's Office
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel risks everything to search the office and finds a deed showing the school purchased the village for nothing after a manufactured 'condemnation.' She is nearly caught by the headmaster's assistant, Ms. Aldous. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the intoxicating, frightening taste of defiance.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel reluctantly allies with Theo, a local boy whose family lost their boats in the takeover, and who has been leaving anonymous notes about the village in the library books. Emotional beat: prickly trust — Hazel learning she can't do this alone.

chapters.title: Key Four: The Chapel Annex
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The fourth key opens the sealed chapel annex, where Hazel finds a page of the recipe hidden in a hymnal — written in Marisol's family's hand, with a marginal note about 'the water that remembers.' Emotional beat: awe and urgency; the recipe is real, and it's a record of memory, not just flour and salt.

chapters.title: Ms. Aldous Knows
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ms. Aldous corners Hazel, not to threaten her but to warn her: the headmaster's family built their legacy on the erasure, and he'll destroy anyone who exposes it — including a missing girl's reputation. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the enemy is a system, not just a man.

chapters.title: What Marisol Was Running From
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, extended flashback. Marisol's grandmother, losing her memory to dementia, gave her the keys and the family's duty: restore the recipe before the last keeper forgets. Marisol went underground when she realized she was being followed. Emotional beat: love as inheritance — duty passed down like a recipe.

chapters.title: Key Five: The flooded Stairwell
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Theo find the fifth key's lock beneath the old stairwell, flooded since the village was drowned. The page inside names the final hiding place: the archive under the gymnasium. Emotional beat: cold dread — the last page lies in the one place Hazel's fear forbids her to go.

chapters.title: Careful Is Another Word for Afraid
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. After a panic attack in the flooded stairwell, Hazel confronts the roots of her hypervigilance with her mother, who admits her own failures. Hazel decides she'd rather drown reaching for something than live carefully forever. Emotional beat: the internal climax — choosing courage over safety.

chapters.title: The Bread That Was Never Eaten
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Theo steal into the kitchen and bake a test loaf from the recovered pages. When Theo's grandmother tastes it, she weeps — remembering her childhood on the drowned street. Emotional beat: revelation that the recipe genuinely carries memory, raising the stakes to something sacred.

chapters.title: Key Six: The Headmaster's Trap
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The sixth key opens the headmaster's private archive, but it's a trap — Ms. Aldous locks them in, revealing the headmaster knew about Marisol all along and let her flee to bury the scandal. Emotional beat: betrayal and despair; the system is always three steps ahead.

chapters.title: The Escape Through the Old Tunnel
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo leads Hazel out through a cannery-era drainage tunnel, his knowledge of the old village saving them. They surface in the cemetery where the founders are buried under unmarked stones. Emotional beat: solidarity — the town's forgotten children carrying each other through its forgotten bones.

chapters.title: Marisol, Found
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Following the seventh key's engraving to a shuttered beach house, Hazel finds Marisol hiding with her grandmother. Marisol confesses she fled rather than fight, ashamed. Hazel refuses to let shame win: 'You started this. I'm not finishing it without you.' Emotional beat: reconciliation and shared resolve.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Gymnasium
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The climax begins: during graduation setup, Hazel, Marisol, and Theo break into the flooded archive beneath the gymnasium. The final page is sealed in a founder's strongbox under rising water. Hazel dives for it as the structure groans. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Almost Drowning
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Trapped briefly underwater, Hazel has a near-death vision of memory itself — the village alive, voices layered like yeast rising. Theo pulls her out. She surfaces clutching the page. Emotional beat: death and rebirth; Hazel's carefulness dies so she can live.

chapters.title: The Loaf at Graduation
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the graduation ceremony, the trio hijacks the bread ritual: Marisol's grandmother recites the recipe's true history as the loaf is baked before the whole town, and the first slice is finally eaten. The headmaster's version of events collapses. Emotional beat: public restoration — memory made flesh and shared.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the aftermath, the school board opens an inquiry, the village is granted memorial status, and Ms. Aldous testifies. The headmaster resigns. Marisol's family is formally recognized as the recipe's keepers. Emotional beat: justice arriving quietly, imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Coral and the Recipe
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On the last day of summer, Hazel, Marisol, and Theo bake bread on the old village foundations, now a memorial garden. Hazel, who once counted exits, now counts people who would come find her. Emotional beat: belonging — inheritance claimed, identity chosen, the careful girl finally at rest.
